capabilities: Escape Markdown trigger characters as you type or paste
Repair the current note, file, or entire vault with idempotent rules
Back up notes before repair and restore previous versions
Suppress Markdown rendering of directives, italics, and == highlights via settings
Skip fenced code blocks, inline code, and genuine link syntax
disambiguation: Not a C++ syntax highlighter or code formatter; it only escapes Markdown trigger characters and repairs the resulting note source.
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README is bilingual (English and Chinese) and includes a detailed changelog and a Limitations section covering frontmatter breakage and Live Preview fence-line behavior.
motivation: The author built it because Markdown's second meaning for C++ characters swallows content into tags, breaks brackets, and turns code notation into emphasis or highlights.
problem: Markdown assigns syntax meaning to characters C++ uses constantly, so angle brackets become HTML tags, array subscripts become links, and == or * create unwanted highlighting and emphasis.

relations.evidence: Or add Yaki-Blake/Cpp-Input-Guard as a beta plugin via BRAT.

summary: Input guard for C++ notes that escapes Markdown trigger characters (<, [, *, _, ==, #include) as you type or paste, and repairs existing notes.
